No code was written and nothing was run, so every step in the plan is still unverified.

**How the plan keeps behaviour unchanged**
Every screen is assigned one of five ways of porting it:
- **Rebuild:** a new screen that reads the same providers. Used for Home, the Motorky list, the reservations list and the loyalty ranks screen.
- **Seam:** the old screen keeps all its state and logic, and only the widget tree it returns is swapped for a plain v2 view. Used for the big logic-heavy screens: booking form, payment, success/result, moto detail, reservation detail and edit, profile, the routes screens, Moje zážitky and ride detail.
- **Variant:** an optional style parameter on a small widget that has its own logic inside (rating card, access codes, booking form sections, FAB strips, error/loading views).
- **Chrome only:** the screen body stays as it is; only the nav, AI button and back control around it change.
- **Keep:** no change at all.

Old screens may also get eight listed refactors that only move existing code into shared functions (PM-1 to PM-8). These are the tab-tap logic, the shell FAB layer and the "paid after restart" listener, the booking-start action from detail, the manual ride toggle, rebook/document/cancel actions, the pending payment/SOS actions, and the Home refresh. Each must be a verbatim move, checked with `git diff --color-moved`.

**Foundation (`lib/core/v2/`)**
The plan lists every file, with these main parts:
- **Kill-switch:** `appV2UiProvider` goes in `feature_flags.dart`. Missing row = on, `false` = off, a fetch error keeps the cached value. A change applies only at cold start or at a safe moment, never while a payment is running.
- **Tokens:** colours including the light surfaces, type scale, spacing, radii, shadows, motion with reduced-motion handling, and a line icon set.
- **Rank theme:**
  - The 20-colour ramp table is copied from `shared/rank-theme.js`, with the solver ported for colours edited in Velín.
  - **Without any SQL**, the app maps the old database colours to the new ramp and leaves manual Velín edits alone.
  - Tier effects, rings, header aura and step marks are included.
- **Widgets:** the full v2 widget set, including:
  - the back/close button in three surface styles;
  - a calendar that paints the whole selected range as one green band;
  - the six result/error templates;
  - a 5-tab nav with a measured label-fit rule so no language overlaps;
  - the AI button with rules that hide it over CTAs;
  - the status strips and `AppShellV2`.

**Per area**
Sections 2.1–2.7 cover Home, catalog/detail/calculator, booking/payment/results, reservations, profile, routes and rides. Each screen has its route and file, technique, new files, the providers and actions it reuses, a checklist of content that must survive, and the states to cover. SOS, login/registration, shop, onboarding and the offline guard keep their current look inside the new chrome.

**Wiring, i18n, tests**
- **Wiring:** three small edits in `main.dart`, and in `router.dart` only the ShellRoute and four screen builders. Route paths, deep links and redirects stay as they are.
- **i18n:** new strings go in `translations_ext_50`–`57`, all prefixed `v2` so they cannot overwrite existing keys, in all 8 languages.
- **Tests:** in `test/v2/`, every new screen and state is pumped in 8 languages at 360×780 and 412×915 and fails on any overflow or exception. A reduced-motion pass must settle (proving no endless animations). PNGs go to the shots folder when `MG_SHOTS_DIR` is set.
- **Extra checks:**
  - **Unit tests:** rank contrast and no purple, nav label fit, and calculator/funnel prices matching the booking form.
  - **Structural tests:** flag off gives the old UI, back is visible everywhere, the AI button never covers a CTA, i18n completeness, file size limits.
  - **Content parity:** every translation key used by an old screen must appear in its v2 version or be on a reviewed waiver list.

Section 6 lists the files nobody may touch, starting with `loyalty_levelup_overlay.dart`, plus 17 risks with mitigations and every shared file touched, for the later iOS port. Section 7 gives the work order: six foundation agents, a first gate, nine area agents, a second gate, then review.

- **Design features the plan leaves out:** these would need new logic, not just a new look:
  - the DESIGN_V22 code requirements C1–C17;
  - live km/time in the recorder (the recorder doesn't expose them);
  - the 30-second GPS wait;
  - a 15 Kč check;

  - "Navigovat sem" on places;

- **Level-up colours:** the celebration will still show the old database rank colours while the rest of v2 shows the new ramp. Making them match means changing the protected overlay or running the ramp SQL, and the SQL waits until both apps ship.
- **Velín toggle:** for a switch in Velín (it only lists rows that already exist), the owner must approve the `app_v2_ui` row migration in section 3.5. It is not needed to ship, because a missing row means on.
- **iOS sync rule:** shipping only Android breaks the CLAUDE.md "same change in both trees" rule for this release. The commit message should record that this was the owner's instruction.

- **`main.dart`:** loads the last known flag value before `runApp`. The router's navigator is wrapped in a new widget, `MgV2Gate` (`lib/core/v2/flag/v2_gate.dart`). I ran verify:render (adversarial) on the Android v2 UI. The v2 look breaks text in every language, and many of the breaks also happen at normal text size, not just with large text. The non-render tests are clean; the new render matrix is not.

**Full test suite:** `flutter test` gives 4807 passed and 0 failed. The 7800 render-matrix tests in it are skipped, because the matrix only runs when `MG_VERIFY_RENDER=1` is set. Log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Vel-n/a6963cc3-5559-53b7-8eeb-5fd2cdb37dae/scratchpad/impl/verify_render/full_suite.txt

**Render matrix:**
- Coverage is 325 v2 screens, sub-states, sheets, dialogs and result/error states, in all 8 languages at 320x690, 360x780 and 412x915.
- Run settings: text scale 1.3, reduced motion on, rank driven by the case.
- The test fails on any FlutterError (overflow or exception), text clipped by an ancestor, text off screen, truncated app copy, a cut price, text overflowing its box, a word split across two lines, nav labels colliding, raw translation keys and fallback-language strings.
- **At 1.3:** 7800 tests, 3818 failed. After removing harness noise, 3751 screen×language×size combinations fail, at 179 source locations.
- **At normal size (1.0, extra pass at 320 and 360):** 5200 tests, 1675 failed. That is 1626 failing combinations at 96 source locations. These are breaks ordinary users see.
- The fails cluster at 320 wide, then 360, then 412 (9857 / 4666 / 1501 findings at 1.3).
- No missing translation keys, raw keys or fallback-language strings were found. The static check confirms every literal v2 key exists in all 8 languages.

**Harness bugs I fixed** (the earlier "all pass in 8 languages" results came from these blind spots):
1. The inspector walked the tree the way semantics does, so it skipped every label inside `ExcludeSemantics` or `Semantics(excludeSemantics:)`. That is most v2 buttons, rows, pills and docks.
2. There was no check for a word split across lines, such as "NAH|RÁV|ÁM".
3. A cut price only counted as minor data truncation.
4. Unclipped horizontal chip rails were reported as clipped.
5. The Riverpod language setting was not set per test, so provider-built texts showed in Czech.
6. The AI button was inspected before it finished moving after a scroll. Re-checked: it does not cover CTAs once settled.
7. Error locations were captured after the widget was gone, so most overflows had no source location.
